knowledge_point.title: Rewriting an Expression Using the Product and Quotient Rules of Logarithms

question.:question/problem: Express $\log\left(5\right)+\log\left(p\right)-\log\left(z\right)$ as a single logarithm. Assume $p>0$ and $z>0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the product rule for logarithms, combine the first two terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\log\left(5\right)+\log\left(p\right)-\log\left(z\right) \\ &=\log\left(5\cdot p\right)-\log\left(z\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Now use the quotient rule to combine the remaining difference:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\log\left(5\cdot p\right)-\log\left(z\right) \\ &=\log\left(\frac{5\cdot p}{z}\right).\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Assume $q>0$.

$\log_{5}\left(\frac{q\cdot 25}{2}\right)=$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the quotient rule for logarithms, separate the numerator and denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\log_{5}\left(\frac{q\cdot 25}{2}\right) \\ &=\log_{5}\left(q\cdot 25\right)-\log_{5}\left(2\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Now use the product rule to expand the logarithm of the numerator:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\log_{5}\left(q\cdot 25\right)-\log_{5}\left(2\right) \\ &=\log_{5}\left(q\right)+\log_{5}\left(25\right)-\log_{5}\left(2\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Since $\log_{5}\left(25\right)=\log_{5}\left(5^{2}\right)=2$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}&\log_{5}\left(q\right)+\log_{5}\left(25\right)-\log_{5}\left(2\right) \\ &=\log_{5}\left(q\right)+2-\log_{5}\left(2\right).\end{aligned}
$$
